question: What percentage of tests will be positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus in the United States for the week ending October 24, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-24 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
I didn't run any news or market searches. The CDC dataset answered most of the questions, so items 3 and 5 below are limited.

**Note on what I used:** The dataset (data.cdc.gov, rgnm-fkqb) only shows its latest release, and that release is dated after 2026-09-14. To stay within the cutoff, I use only weeks that would have been published by 2026-09-14. That means 2026 weeks through the week ending 2026-09-05 (released around 2026-09-11), plus earlier years. I ignore any later weeks or values. Recent weeks can be revised slightly between releases.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the national rhinovirus/enterovirus (RV/EV) "percent_pos" value for the week ending 2026-10-24, in the release dated 2026-10-30. Each row has the week-ending date, the number of tests and detections, the percent positive, and the release date. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Latest week available by the cutoff: the week ending 2026-09-05, at **28.07%** positive (16,874 tests). [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The target week is about 7 weeks after the latest available data.
- 2026 is in its usual late-summer rise as schools reopen. Percent positive by week ending:
  - 2026-08-08: 14.70%
  - 2026-08-15: 16.94%
  - 2026-08-22: 21.03%
  - 2026-08-29: 24.83%
  - 2026-09-05: 28.07%

  [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Spring 2026 had its own peak of 26.07% (week ending 2026-05-09), then a summer low of about 13.75% (week ending 2026-07-18).

## 3. Recent news
- I didn't search news outlets. I found no unusual RV/EV development (such as an EV-D68 outbreak) in the data I reviewed. Rising test volumes (about 13,100 in early August to 16,900 by 2026-09-05) fit the normal back-to-school pattern.

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
The usual pattern: positivity rises fast from mid-August, peaks around 29 to 32% in mid-to-late September, then falls slowly through October.

Values from about this week of the year to about the target week ([data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)):

| Year | Early Sept | Peak | Late Oct (target week) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 24.21% (09-04) | 27.82% (10-09) | 25.93% (10-23) | +1.7 pts |
| 2022 | 31.73% (09-03) | 32.46% (09-24) | 24.72% (10-22) | -7.0 pts |
| 2023 | 27.40% (09-02) | 29.61% (09-23) | 24.51% (10-21) | -2.9 pts |
| 2024 | 25.84% (09-07); 30.26% (09-14) | 30.63% (09-21) | 25.82% (10-26) | 0 pts (-4.4 from 09-14) |
| 2025 | 29.51% (09-06) | 30.66% (09-20) | 24.58% (10-25) | -4.9 pts |

- Around the target week (late October) in 2021 to 2025, values fell between 24.5% and 25.9%. That is a narrow band of about 1.4 points.
- The change from early September to late October ranged from +1.7 to -7.0 points. The median was about -3 points.
- 2026 compared with past years:
  - At 28.07% in the week ending 2026-09-05, 2026 is a little below 2025 (29.51%) and 2022 (31.73%).
  - It is above 2021 (24.21%), 2023 (27.40%) and 2024 (25.84%).
  - The rise started a little later than in 2025. In 2026 it reached 21% in the week ending 08-22, against 24.26% in 2025's week ending 08-23.
- Early-September values can dip around the Labor Day week, as in 2023 when it went from 27.40% to 26.08%.
- Test volume (about 17,000 a week) is a bit lower than in fall 2025 (about 19,000 to 20,000).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I didn't search Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold, and I don't know of any market on this series. CDC does not publish forecasts for RV/EV positivity.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly data releases on Fridays from 2026-09-18 to 2026-10-30. Each one will show whether 2026 peaks in mid-to-late September as usual.
- Possible risks:
  - An EV-D68 surge (these have tended to come in even years, but did not appear clearly in 2022 or 2024).
  - Competition from other viruses: rising flu, RSV or COVID positivity in October can coincide with lower RV/EV positivity.
  - Changes in testing volume or which labs report.
  - Revisions to recent weeks between releases.
- Weather: rhinovirus is driven mainly by schools reopening rather than weather, so I didn't look up a seasonal weather outlook.

Sources:
- [CDC NREVSS percent positivity dataset rgnm-fkqb (data.cdc.gov)](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
